content: S1: the loop owns dispatch, so one flow of work replaces the orchestration (plans/task-flow.md S1). The wake landed 2026-10-03 (9aef0cbb): a write that makes a row ready wakes its headless holder, and the handoff needs no verb of its own. Gate: one fan-out run by hand, on the loop alone.

records.result: Landed 2026-10-03. The run's end now takes its members: end_spent_runs hangs off the same TodoUpdated arm as the wake, ends a run whose rows are all gone through the one end_session (extracted from the stop path), and only ever ends headless members the run spawned, so a session a person sits in is never reaped. Checked: 394 kcode-app-core server tests pass, a_spent_run_takes_only_the_sessions_it_spawned pins the selection, clippy clean on the changed files. What I did not check: the live fan-out, which is t3 and waits for the next build. Also correcting this row: the idle members seen on 2026-10-03 sat there while the run still had open rows, which is by design (a member's session outlives its turn so it can be handed more rows); the case fixed here is the run whose rows are all closed leaving its members alive forever.

Landed in four commits, 1,915 lines gone: 9ddcd773 the action, 37c56551 the card, 738c8784 the driver and its policies, 5e5813c8 the claim, with cf559947 for the formatting the scripted deletions broke. Nothing else in the tree named the driver, and the file compiles with no dead code.

Subsumed by S1b, not done separately. auto_assign_claims and its 15 s TTL are used only by the assign path's target selection (comm_control.rs:279 and :478, both inside the assign handlers), so deleting the verbs deletes the claim map with them. Nothing else claims a target: the loop picks the rows the session holds, and the holder write is the model's.

Subsumed by S1b, not done separately. The dispatch-time liveness predicate is the inlined rule inside next_dispatch (comm_control.rs:355), which S1b deletes. The sweep's predicate (salvage_dead_assignees, swarm.rs:567) is then the only copy, so the disagreement the braid note recorded resolves by deletion rather than by a new assignee_is_dead.

content: S1k the gate: one fan-out run, end to end, on the loop alone, by hand on the user's own socket, on the next build. A root grants, spawns two workers, hands them rows, the workers close, the root integrates and closes the anchor, and no member session outlives the anchor. If it fails, stop and report; do not patch around it. Also listed in docs/dev/testing.md under the by-hand smoke list.

S1b delete the assign verbs end to end: the three tool actions (assign_task, assign_next, fill_slots) with their schema entries and the "assign" alias, their helpers in tool/communicate.rs (assign_task_to_session, spawn_assignment_session, resolve_run_plan_concurrency and its call site), the two wire requests with their responses and the request arms in client_lifecycle and client_lightweight_control, and the assign machinery behind them in server/comm_control.rs (handle_comm_assign_task, handle_comm_assign_task_with_mode, handle_comm_assign_next, next_dispatch, the target resolvers, spawn_assigned_task_run, the turn-end auto-complete) with comm_control_tests. What replaces them is the loop's dispatch: a holder write plus the wake a turn that already ended uses, and the wake landed 2026-10-03. Scoping found that this closure contains two rows' work: auto_assign_claims and its 15 s TTL (S1h), and the dispatch-time liveness predicate (S1i), so S1b takes both.

S1c delete the read views and the report action: status, summary, report, plan_status, read_context, resync_plan, task_graph, expand_node, complete_node (tool/communicate.rs:2391-2646), and the instruction protocol around them (the spawn reminder, the assignment suffix, the tldr rule, the notification advice text).

S1d the verbs decide to four: spawn, stop, list_models and one message verb. stop becomes subtree-scoped (a session and its descendants on the spawn edge) and keeps stop_swarm_sessions its one caller; retry, wake, cleanup and cleanup_swarm_workers go with the action (tool/communicate.rs:2504-2527, 2846-2876).

S1e delete the durable waiter with await_members: comm_await.rs (664), await_members_state.rs (278), the SwarmAwaitCompleted bus event with its background_tasks delivery, and the request; readiness is the wait. Note what that leaves behind: run_plan was one of the two producers of a swarm-flavored background task, so await_members is the last, and after this the card's swarm flavor has no producer (the tool_name == "swarm" branches in kcode-tui/src/tui/ui_messages.rs:1513, :1528, :1798 and their two fixtures). S2's renderer cut should take them, or S1e should.

S1f delete the channels and the shared-context KV store: share, share_append, read, broadcast, dm, channel, list_channels, channel_members, subscribe_channel, unsubscribe_channel, with the store and the channel index.

S1l the bound (a decision): one admission cap read where a spawn or a wake is admitted (MAX_SWARM_MEMBERS=1000 hard, agents.swarm_max_concurrent_agents=32 soft, both read today only on the spawn path at comm_session.rs:1227-1249); run_plan's recovery dance dies with the driver; the credential-wave breaker becomes a provider-health signal that fails a turn with a clear error.
